statement: In 5 of 12 books with a problem an adult makes the resolution possible (a tickle, an injection, a 'yes', a repairer called, a mother's instruction); in 7 the child or a peer resolves it.

scope.population: contemporary open-licence picture books: Book Dash (13), African Storybook (2), StoryWeaver/Pratham Books (1); 2014-2025

analyst_note:
2026-10-14: Best Friends and An Unexpected Adventure (wordless) reviewed for this claim. Best Friends: the teacher only suggests; a classmate's invitation and the protagonist's own choice resolve it (counterexample). An Unexpected Adventure has no problem to resolve and is not counted.
2026-10-15: Not counted (no problem to resolve): Bathtub Safari, Khumo, Ga Mohana. Book Dash: Zuko supports (Gogo phones a repairer), Come Back Cat and Feathered Friends contradict. African Storybook: Chicken and Millipede supports (Mother Millipede tells him what to do); Bohlale contradicts (Gogo only names what the child already did). StoryWeaver: Monu tames the monsters alone.

magicpaper.current: MagicPaper beats favour the child acting (take_charge, find_own_courage)
magicpaper.suggested: No change; record that adult-enabled endings are common in this population, and track agency as the corpus grows.
